sources.title: BRAHUI
sources.locator: Ethnography and language overview: Brahui communities principally in Pakistani Baluchistan; Dravidian basis of Brahui; historical discussion of settlement, literature and multilingual language use.

sources.title: INDO-IRANIAN FRONTIER LANGUAGES
sources.locator: Overview of Pakistan's western/northern multilingual setting, including Brahui alongside Balochi, Pashto, Urdu and other regional languages; used as context for language contact rather than as an ethnic generalization.

whoTheyAre.summary: The current PeopleGroups.org record identifies Brahui in Pakistan and ties the record to Brahui (brh). Glottolog and Encyclopaedia Iranica independently identify Brahui as a Dravidian language and document a long multilingual setting in Pakistani Baluchistan.

religionAndCommunity.summary: PeopleGroups.org supplies an aggregate Sunni Islam label for this source record. It remains a provider-level mission-research classification and is not a statement about every Brahui person's belief or practice.

profile.whyUnreachedIntro: This candidate keeps the mission classification tied to PeopleGroups.org fields. Brahui ethnicity, multilingualism, regional history and religion are not treated as causes of unreached status.

whyUnreached.heading: Current source mission status
whyUnreached.summary: PeopleGroups.org currently reports PG006335 below the 2% evangelical threshold with GSEC 1 and no recent church-planting activity while its SPI presentation is Engaged yet Unreached.

whyUnreached.heading: Reported resources stay source-specific
whyUnreached.summary: The provider currently lists a Brahui JESUS film and Bible-resource surfaces; the candidate does not infer how widely any resource is distributed, understood or used.

claims.text: The current PeopleGroups.org profile PG006335 identifies the people-group record as Brahui in Pakistan and lists Brahui (brh) as its primary language.
claims.interpretationNote: The public profile establishes PGID/name/country/language alignment; the guarded maintainer review must re-fetch the live record and verify PEID before publication.

claims.text: Glottolog and Encyclopaedia Iranica independently classify Brahui as a Dravidian language; Glottolog assigns ISO 639-3 code brh and glottocode brah1256.

Reference scholarship places Brahui in a historically multilingual region where Brahui, Balochi, Urdu and other languages have interacted; older ethnographic descriptions document substantial bilingualism, so a single primary-language label should not be read as exclusive language use.
claims.interpretationNote: The detailed bilingualism evidence in the Iranica Brahui article is historical and is not presented as a current percentage or as universal for every Brahui community.

claims.text: The current PeopleGroups.org Brahui of Pakistan profile reports Sunni Islam as its aggregate primary-religion label.
claims.interpretationNote: This is a provider classification for PG006335, not a statement about every Brahui person's belief or practice.

claims.text: PeopleGroups.org currently reports less than 2% evangelical presence and no recent church-planting activity for PG006335, and its profile presents the record as Engaged yet Unreached.
claims.interpretationNote: These are source-native mission-research fields for one people-group-in-country record, not a judgment about individuals.

claims.text: The current PeopleGroups.org profile lists one JESUS film on its Brahui resource surface and provides linked Bible-resource surfaces, while its Faith Comes by Hearing section currently lists no Bible resource entry for the language.
claims.interpretationNote: These are provider resource-surface observations; they do not establish overall Scripture availability, distribution, comprehension or use.
